pll1d37c9-d1e3501.summary: Affirms that the divine nature is nowhere absent, contained in no place, reaching from end to end (Wis 8:1) by immensity and immobility rather than extension or motion.
claims: God reaches all things by immensity and immobility, not by extension or local motion.

pll1d37c9-d1e3515.summary: Augustine's analogy of wisdom in two wise men: God is wholly in heaven, wholly on earth, wholly in both, contained by no place.
claims: God is not diffused through things as a spread-out magnitude.
God is wholly in each place and contained by none.

pll1d37c9-d1e3534.summary: Augustine on the Psalms: the Word is everywhere by himself, not in parts, reaching from end to end not by local motion but by immobility.
claims: The Word is everywhere without being in part or moving locally.

pll1d37c9-d1e3559.summary: Summary: God is everywhere by essence without being diffused by magnitude or moving from place to place.
claims: God is everywhere by essence without diffusion or motion.

pll1d37c9-d1e3562.summary: Augustine, 83 Questions: God is not somewhere, since what is somewhere is contained and is body; rather all things are in him, without his being a place; the temple of God is improperly called his place.
claims: God is not in any place; all things are in him.
God is not a place in the way a body's extension is.

pll1d37c9-d1e3583.summary: Clarifies the statement: God is not in place localiter, i.e., without circumscription or local motion.
claims: God is in place but not locally.

pll1d37c9-d1e3586.summary: Objection: new creatures come to be in which God begins to be; hence God seems to be where he was not and thus mutable.
claims: Objection: God's being in newly created things implies change in God.

pll1d37c9-d1e3589.summary: Reply: God begins or ceases to be in creatures without changing himself, just as with the world; it is the creature or place that begins or ceases, not God who leaves.
claims: Change in God's presence to things derives from change in creatures, not in God.

pll1d37c9-d1e3592.summary: Closing summary: the digression on things in God and God in all arose from the discussion of God's knowledge, prompted by the question whether all things are in God because he knows them.
claims: The treatment of divine presence arose incidentally from the discussion of divine knowledge and wisdom.

pl-l1d37c9.summary: Closes the treatment of God's omnipresence by insisting God is everywhere without extension or local motion, by immensity and immobility of essence. Uses Augustine's analogies of shared wisdom and Wisdom 8:1, affirms 'in God' over 'in place', answers the objection that God's coming to be in new creatures implies change, and ends by recalling the digression's origin in God's knowledge.
claims: God is wholly everywhere without spatial extension or local motion.
God is not in place locally; rather all things are in God.
God's beginning to be in new creatures involves no change in God.
The digression arose from the question whether things are 'in God' by his knowledge of them.
